### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `084af0baf71dfbfaf5537ebadfd7c5f77605ce3f` — the merge of head `476460a86c89fccb17e4dd9173d5a4165722edd7` into base `42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 084af0baf71dfbfaf5537ebadfd7c5f77605ce3f && git checkout 084af0baf71dfbfaf5537ebadfd7c5f77605ce3f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a 476460a86c89fccb17e4dd9173d5a4165722edd7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a && git merge --no-ff 476460a86c89fccb17e4dd9173d5a4165722edd7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 42b60b91bdee4963a3a64be57f71d729946d649a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `476460a86c89fccb17e4dd9173d5a4165722edd7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.exposure.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.record-resource-exposure.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.merged-object-reads.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-package-object-discovery.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`objectPackageDisabledError`, `isObjectOfDisabledPackage`, `isItemOfDisabledPackage`, `getMetaItems` / `readFlattenedMetaItems`, `getMetaItem` / `getMetaItemForExecution` / `readMetaItemFace`, `assertObjectRegistered`, `metadataStoreUnavailableError`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts (the `protocol` slot's registration), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`readExposureDeclaration`, `refuseUnexposedDataAction`, `callData`, `refuseUnservedRelationTargets`), packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts (`readMergedItems`, `listObjectSummaries`, `listObjectsDiagnosed`, `describeObject`), packages/runtime/src/api-exposure.ts (`checkApiExposure`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`objectItemReader`, `enforceApiAccess`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`loadObjectItem`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`list_objects`, `describe_object`, `validate_expression`, `isSystemObject`, `errorResultWithCode`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts beyond its hunk (`bridgeResources`, the three `objectstack://objects` resolvers), packages/mcp/src/index.ts and packages/mcp/package.json (the `exports` map), packages/mcp/src/metadata-completeness.ts (`diagnoseObjectListRead`), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (the stdio principal), .github/workflows/ci.yml (the `dogfood` job's `if:`, the Test Core shard exclusion, the `dogfood-gate` contract), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`CATEGORIES`); .changeset/25138-mcp-stdio-package-objects.md for ② only

Inputs: card #25138 (body; pointer 6328231985; claim 6341568965; `os-dev-report` 6343835289, read as claims), PR #25243 (body, nine-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `123ff6f4e2`), and the 42 check-runs on the head: 35 `success`, 7 `skipped` (the dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, Console Pin Gate, the 18.x upgrade harness, the packed-tarball smoke), 0 `failure`; the five required contexts (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core with its six shards, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard) are `success`, as are Check Changeset, the two claim guards and the single-writer guard. Prior records read because the card cites them: PR #25136's body and its records 6328012432 (FAIL on `d19b65bf1c`) and 6329661857 (PASS on `c0fb1c715f`). No governed path is in the file list. The face is the PR body's and the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Every line number below is read at the head sha.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Discovery reads the protocol's merged listing, through the one unwrap, and `list_objects` / `describe_object` cannot disagree — RIGHT.** `readMergedObjects` (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts:373-377`) asks `protocol.getMetaItems({ type: 'object' })` and unwraps it with `metaItemsArray` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:535-539`), the function the skill read on this transport already uses (`:580`). `listObjects` (`stdio-data-bridge.ts:843-844`) reads `metadataService.listObjects()` only when that returns `undefined`, which happens on structural absence alone (no `protocol` slot, or one without `getMetaItems`); a throw has no catch and travels. `listObjectsDiagnosed` (`:863-864`) composes over `bridge.listObjects()` and asks only the verdict of `diagnoseObjectListRead(metadataService)`, so the shared tool's preferred path (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:704-705`) renders the merged listing with the copy's `partial` verdict — the composition the card asked for. `describeObject` (`:873-876`) reads the same listing per call, and `validate_expression` reads `describeObject` (`mcp-http-tools.ts:793`), so every listed object is describable and a name the listing omits is "not found" on all three tools. The listing is the one REST serves: `getMetaItems` is `readFlattenedMetaItems` on the served face (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:10007-10019`), which omits a disabled package's items by `isItemOfDisabledPackage` (`:10615-10617`, predicate `:552-555`), the same read the HTTP bridge's `readMergedItems` makes (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:454-471`, `:599-600`). The slot the plugin resolves is the full `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` that `assembleMetadataProtocol` registers under `'protocol'` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts:250-255`), the one seam ObjectQLPlugin's built-in mode and MetadataProtocolPlugin share, so it carries the listing and both by-name faces. `sys_` objects are withheld by the shared tool (`mcp-http-tools.ts:286-288`), narrower than REST, exactly as on HTTP. Noted, not blocking, as on the HTTP record: `describe_object` reads and decorates the whole served listing where a by-name read would read one object — a cost, not a contract change.

2. **The gate's healthy by-name read is the HTTP twin's and REST's — RIGHT.** `readObjectDeclaration` (`stdio-data-bridge.ts:337-355`) selects `getMetaItemForExecution`, else `getMetaItem`, else the copy (`:344`), and accepts the item only under its own name (`:353`): line for line `readExposureDeclaration` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:346-371`) and `RestServer.objectItemReader` with `loadObjectItem`'s own-name rule (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2570-2586`; `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:491-497`). `readMetaItemFace` (`protocol.ts:11422-11428`) shares every source and merge between the two faces and differs only in the serving decorations, so the definition this gate judges is the one REST's gate judges. `enforceApiExposure` then applies the same two codes REST and `callData` answer: `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` (`:463-469`) and `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` with the effective set (`:477-482`), unchanged since #8083.

3. **`OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` is thrown, nowhere swallowed — RIGHT; the defect record 6328012432 found on the HTTP twin is not copied.** The protocol raises it from both by-name faces for an object of a disabled package (`protocol.ts:11426-11428`, constructor `:519-528`, predicate `:536-539`). `readObjectDeclaration` rethrows it before its fallback (`stdio-data-bridge.ts:349`), `enforceApiExposure` rethrows it past its fail-open catch (`:450`), both on the `code` alone (`:295-297`), the mechanism `callData`'s `'refuse'` arm uses (`action-execution.ts:365`, `:445-447`, `:471`). Every door asks the gate before any engine call: the six verbs (`:898`, `:927`, `:941`, `:964`, `:994`, `:1010`) and the record resource (`packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts:768`). The engine asks no disabled-package predicate (record 6329661857, judgment 1; unchanged), so this gate is the only refusal on a transport whose every verb is engine-only, and it is now there on all seven doors. Swallow audit of the three remaining catches and reads: `enforceRelationTargetExposure`'s catch (`:508-511`) swallows a throw from the ADDRESSED object's read, but the gate at `:898` / `:1010` has already thrown for that object one line earlier, and each target's gate (`:514`) rethrows; the two write-response strips (`:955`, `:987`) read after the gate on the same object and have no catch, so a throw there is an error, never a served response. The tool layer renders `code` and `status` off any thrown value (`mcp-http-tools.ts:367-370`), and the record resource renders `{ error, code, status }` the same way (`mcp-server-runtime.ts:1264-1292`), which is the envelope both pin files assert. Against REST: `loadObjectItem` reads the refusal as "no object" (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:500`) and the data plane refuses next (`assertObjectRegistered`, `protocol.ts:12916`); on stdio the tool input schema runs before the bridge and nothing stands between the gate and the engine, so there is no refusal order to keep, and a well-formed request gets REST's answer: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, the engine never asked. No refusal's status moves.

4. **An outage of either protocol read never widens exposure — RIGHT.** By-name: a protocol without the read judges the copy (`:344`); any throw but the refusal judges the copy (`:350`), the source this gate read on every request before the move; a throwing copy read reaches `:451` and falls open, the pre-move answer. So on every input the outage answer equals the pre-move answer and cannot allow what the pre-move gate refused; REST fails open at once on the same throw (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:501-507`), so this door is at most REST's exposure then. Listing: a throw travels to the client with no fallback to the un-merged listing (`:373-377`, `:843`, `:873`), rendered as the protocol's `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`metadataStoreUnavailableError`, `protocol.ts:4329-4338`) through `errorResultWithCode` — what `GET /api/v1/meta/object` answers. Carried from record 6329661857, non-blocking: on the no-copy shape the by-name fallback is a silent fail-open indistinguishable from health; a one-shot warn would make a persistent outage visible on exactly the card's shape.

5. **The accessor resolved per use returns the bridge's own kernel's protocol — RIGHT.** `protocolReads` (`plugin.ts:714-721`) asks `ctx.getService('protocol')` at each use and answers `undefined` on absence or throw; the same `ctx` resolves `metadata` (`:410`) and `objectql` (`:485`), so the engine, the copy and the protocol are one kernel's services, and on an `environmentId` kernel the protocol is the one assembled over that same `ql` with that `environmentId`. A slot filled with a partial object is probed per read (`:344`, `:375`) and falls to the copy, as before. A `replaceService('protocol')` after `start()` is seen by the accessor and not by the captured engine and copy: the direction the dev chose on purpose (the HTTP bridge resolves per request too), and it cannot widen, since an absent or throwing slot reads the copy. `StdioProtocolObjectReads` (`stdio-data-bridge.ts:140-148`) is the narrow duck type; the real signatures are assignable.

6. **The relation-target gate and the write-response strip read the judged definition — RIGHT, with one divergence named precisely.** `enforceRelationTargetExposure` (`:498-514`) finds a package object's condition sites where it has no copy, and refuses each target with the gate's own codes (`:514`), so an unexposed target is refused as the data door refuses it (#22777). The disabled-package arm: a condition whose target belongs to a disabled package is refused `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` here, where the HTTP bridge's `refuseUnservedRelationTargets` reads the target through `resolveWriteResponseSchema` and asks `checkApiExposure` alone (`action-execution.ts:227-243`) and REST's gate reads the refusal as absence, so neither twin raises it for a target. On that one input stdio refuses what the twins would let the engine read to lower the condition: a narrowing of stdio alone, in the refusing direction, with the code REST gives the same object when addressed; the dev's note says "stricter than REST" and it is stricter than the HTTP bridge too. Code-read, not pinned (the unit pin's target is an `apiEnabled: false` one). Non-blocking; carried. The strips (`:955`, `:987`) now read the definition the gate judged, closing the echo of an `internal: true` field on the no-copy shape in passing; pinned in both files.

7. **The `isSystem` bypass — residual, pre-existing, not widened.** `:443` returns before the read for a system principal, the bypass the HTTP gate shares; the stdio principal comes from `resolveStdioExecutionContext` (`plugin.ts:249-262`, `resolveAuthzContext` over the key row) and `plugin.ts` sets no `isSystem`. The unit pin names the bypass. Carried as record 6329661857 carried it.

8. **Public surface — RIGHT, none moves.** `metaItemsArray` becomes an export of `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (`:535`), and `enforceApiExposure`'s first parameter and the two new interfaces are exports of `stdio-data-bridge.ts`; `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` re-exports none of them (it exports `MCPServerPlugin`, `MCPServerRuntime`, the two tool registrars, the skill helpers and the connect UI), and the package's `exports` map is `.` alone, resolving to `dist/index.*`. By the published-surface rule (the `exports` map decides), nothing published moves. No import cycle: `mcp-server-runtime.ts` imports nothing from `stdio-data-bridge.ts`. `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/rest` are untouched; the `metadata` service gets no second copy, as the card required.

9. **Pins, and what the check-runs measured — read as claims where CI did not execute them.** The 39-case unit file ran in Test Core (six shards `success`; Test Core excludes `@objectstack/dogfood`, `ci.yml:711`), and its cases cover each branch of the two reads named in the PR body. The 70-case dogfood file did NOT execute in any check-run on this head: the `dogfood` job is deny-listed on `pull_request` and `merge_group` events (`ci.yml:2037`, the #22998 two-speeds contract), and the `Dogfood Regression Gate` context concludes `success` with zero expected attestations by design (`ci.yml:109-112`). Read at the head, the file's rows match the PR's table (four shapes × 10 rows; a disabled package × 15 rows on two shapes), drive the real `MCPServerPlugin` stdio session over an in-process JSON-RPC transport, assert the coded envelope on every refusal, and spy the seven engine methods for "never reached". Its execution on this head rests on the dev's report: 70/70 on `eb3b93d9bd` and the full battery on `1261513f93`, the two later commits touching one unit file and the ledger. The push that lands this PR runs the full battery, where a red is the lane's main-red. Not a blocker; named so the seat knows which pin CI has and has not run.

10. **The engine-double ledger — RIGHT.** The three `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` rows record the new unit double's `findOne` / `update` / `delete`, which open with the shared `assertEngine*` asserts (unit file `:83-94`); they are what `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write` emits, and the gate ran green inside Lint & Repo Gates.

Verdict on the face: every change narrows or holds; no public surface moves; the one widening the HTTP review found on the twin is absent here, by the same mechanism that closed it there. This head is the narrowing its `Clause-②` line declares.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/mcp': patch`, with the BREAKING banner, the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker comment (a member of `CATEGORIES`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:536-543`, in the marker form `:62-63`), and both declaration lines, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body. Right: a `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and a non-protocol change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3); `none` is right because no authorable key, accepted value or default moves (an `enable.apiEnabled` / `enable.apiMethods` the author already wrote is enforced where it was not read, and an operator's package switch is honoured on one more door); the only published package the diff moves is `@objectstack/mcp`. Check Changeset is `success` on the head. The marker's own prose matches the diff (nothing exported is removed or narrowed; no stored shape moves).

Sentence by sentence: the title — true, modulo the pre-existing `sys_` withholding of the `list_objects` tool (`allowSystemObjects` defaults to false), which the PR body's contract item 1 states precisely ("the non-`sys_` set"); non-blocking. "Before" — true: discovery read the copy; `describe_object` and `validate_expression` both read `describeObject`; the verbs were served because the gate read the absent copy as "no declaration"; `update_record` / `delete_record` reached the engine through `findById`; the strip read the absent copy and masked nothing. "Now" — true (judgments 1, 2, 6). "Also changed" — true: the listing omits a disabled package's objects (`protocol.ts:10615-10617`); every verb and the resource refuse `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` (judgment 3); the listing's `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` travels (judgment 4). "Unchanged" — true (judgments 4, 5). "What to do" — prescriptive and consistent with the codes. No model identifier in the changeset, the PR body or the six commits, whose trailer pair is the model-free form.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report 6343835289: `open_questions` is empty — nothing to answer.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered or escalated:
1. The stdio schema resources `objectstack://objects` and `objectstack://objects/NAME` read the `metadata` service — confirmed at the head (`mcp-server-runtime.ts:897`, `:809`). On the no-copy shape the two resources now list and describe fewer objects than the tools on the same transport (an under-serving of schema, no record and no data verb behind it), and on the copying shape they still list a disabled package's objects, as they did before this PR. Not a widening; a new tool-versus-resource inconsistency on this transport. ESCALATED: the seat files it from the report's dedupe words; the record resource, which this PR does gate, is not part of it.
2. Carrier none: (a) the relation-target refusal stricter than REST — judged in ① 6, and stricter than the HTTP bridge as well; carried for parity on the next touch of either side; (b) the internal-field strip leak closed in passing — right, pinned; (c) `describe_object` reads the whole listing per call — a cost, as on HTTP; noted.

The PR body's Acceptance notes, each judged: the two above; "describe reads the whole listing" — noted; **file surface** — the claim names `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, its tests under `packages/mcp/src/` and one changeset, with "stop on breach"; the diff also touches `plugin.ts` (the accessor wiring, without which the real plugin hands the bridge no protocol and the fix is inert), `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (one in-package export so the two merged reads on this transport share one unwrap), the dogfood pin (where the stdio exposure twin already lives, and the only real-kernel row) and the gate-written ledger. Each is load-bearing for the claimed fix, inside the lane's package or a gate's own output, and none is governed (Queue Guard and the single-writer guard are `success`). The dev did not stop; it explained in the PR body rather than in the report. Right on the contract face; the process deviation is the seat's to note. **Branch name** — AGENTS.md (Multi-agent discipline 2) names `claude/issue-NNNN-slug`; this head is on `claude/project-thread-dkk3hd`. The claim comment names that branch and "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is `success`, so ownership is recorded; the consequences are that the `issue-25138` pre-check cannot find this head and that the branch never meets condition ① of the force-with-lease rule. Not a contract matter; non-blocking; the seat records it. **Deviation** (dispatch marks written through the session's MCP tools as `os-sales` before the relay was found) — outside the contract face; the seat's.

New from this review, non-blocking, to carry: (1) the dogfood pin is unexecuted by CI on this head by design (① 9) — the landing push's full battery is where it first runs under CI; (2) a one-shot warn on the no-copy outage fall-open (① 4), the same note the HTTP record carried; (3) relation-target parity between the three doors on a disabled package's target (① 6); (4) the `isSystem` residual (① 7).
